newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: OPPOSITION PRESSURES GOVT OVER HOLLOWS JOB OFFER
Federal Labor MP Lyndsay Tanner says the Government has been too hasty in clearing two ministers of wrongdoing over a job offer to Gabi Hollows.
The Opposition claims an offer to Ms Hollows of a job in Aboriginal health was conditional on her giving up a Government appointment to the Civil Aviation Safety Authority Board.
The Prime Minister says legal advice on a letter from Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron to Ms Hollows, containing the job offer, shows there was no breach of the Crimes Act.

But Mr Tanner says Mr Howard's legal advice should have covered discussions involving Gabi Hollows, Transport minister, John Sharp, who recommended the appointment, and Senator Herron. Deputy Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, says he's confident no inducement was offered to Ms Hollows and the Opposition is grasping at straws.
JOBLESS RATE EXPECTED TO COME IN UNCHANGED
Australia's jobless rate is generally expected to remain unchanged when January's official measure of the labour force is released later this morning.
The median forecast among financial market economists is for a national jobless rate of 8.6 percent.
That's despite what's expected to be growth of around 10,000 in the number of Australians with a job.
TRANSPORT WAGE HEARING TO CONTINUE TODAY
A union wage hearing will continue in the Industrial Relations Commission in Melbourne today.
A small transport company is labelling the Workplace Relations Act as unworkable, saying the Federal Government's interpretation is wrong.
Tasmanian firm, Shorthaul Limited, wants the union's 11-per cent wage claim and award change granted with productivity trade-offs.
Manager, David Bean, believes earlier comments by the Industrial Relations Minister, Peter Reith, that smaller operators are being forced to support the claim, are way off.
Mr Bean says the government's enterprise bargaining system has failed small transport companies.
MORE ANTHRAX CASES IN VICTORIA
Another three herds have been infected with Anthrax in Victoria's Goulburn Valley.
In the two weeks since the first cattle died, the deaths have risen to 72 in 34 herds, in the area between Tatura and Stanhopoe.
The Natural Resources Department has vaccinated nearly 10-thousand stock on almost one hundred dairy farms.
One man, employed in a Stanhope knackery, who tested positive to Anthrax, is receiving specialist treatment in the Goulburn Valley Base Hospital at Shepparton.
MCDONALDS ALLOWED IN TO PORT DOUGLAS
Despite some stiff local opposition, fast food chain McDonalds has been been given permission to build in Port Douglas, in far north Queensland.
McDonalds has been at the centre of a fight over a restaurant site in the town, which has proven popular with pop stars, prime ministers and presidents.
Locals say the image portrayed by McDonalds is not in keeping with the spirit of Port Douglas.
But the council voted six to one to allow McDonalds in.
Councillor Earle Bailey, who voted against the company, admits the council had little choice because the land is already zoned for restaurant use.
MPs PROPOSE OFFSHORE AIRPORT FOR SYDNEY
Three Federal Liberal MPs want the Government to investigate an offshore airport for Sydney.
The three backbenchers, Paul Zammit, Jackie Kelly and Dana Vale, have electorates affected by plans for a second airport.
They say an off-shore airport would avoid the need for an airport at either Badgery's Creek or Holsworthy and would mean Kingsford Smith airport could then be phased out early next century.
The MPs say it would not be a floating airport, it would be built on piers sunk into the sandstone bedrock of the Continental shelf off Sydney's southern coastline.
ALLENBY LOOKING FORWARD TO TIGER CHALLENGE
In golf, the Australian Masters gets underway at Huntingdale in Melbourne today.
Robert Allenby, who along with fellow Australian Brett Ogle has been drawn to play Tiger Woods for the first two rounds, says he's looking forward to going head-to-head with the American Champion.
Allenby says he's played with Woods before, at the Scottish Open two years ago.
